statements.claim: The garden attached to Bhanu's women's quarters was unapproachable and stood unguarded while the Yadava heroes were busy with their sports, the moment Nikumbha chose to strike.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237: 'Although the garden, attached to the female appartment of Bhanu, was unapproachable, still at that time there were no guards for the Yadavas were busy with their sports.'

statements.claim: Years before, Pradyumna had carried off Prabhavati, daughter of Nikumbha's brother Vajranabha, and the demon had never forgiven the insult.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237: 'the daughter of his brother Vajranabha, by name Prabhavati, had been taken away by Pradyumna... Remembering this former enmity.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha slipped into the garden and seized Bhanumati, the beautiful daughter of Bhanu.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237: 'stole away the beautiful daughter of Bhanu by name Bhanumati.'

statements.claim: On hearing the lamentation Vasudeva and Ahuka rushed out in fury, found no offender, and went to Krishna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (7-8): 'the heroes, Vasudeva and Ahuka issued out, filled with wrath. And not seeing the offender before them... went where the highly powerful Krishna was.'

statements.claim: Krishna mounted Garuda with Arjuna beside him and ordered Pradyumna, whose banner bore the makara, to follow in his chariot.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (9-10): 'rode, together with Partha, Garuda... Having commanded the hero having the emblem of a Makara on his flag to follow him on his car.'

statements.claim: They overtook Nikumbha before he could reach the city of Vajra and the safety of his kinsmen.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (11): 'before Nikumbha... could reach the city of Vajra, Partha and Krishna... overtook him in the way.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha fought smiling, a heavy club in his right hand and the weeping Bhanumati in his left, so none could strike him in earnest.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (13-15): 'Nikumbha... smilingly fought with them all with heavy clubs. Holding the maiden Bhanumati by his left hand... hurled the club with his right hand.'

statements.claim: Krishna, Pradyumna and Arjuna, though capable of slaying the demon, could not bear to wound the maiden.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (16): 'although capable of slaying that irrepressible enemy they began to sigh piteously out of their excessive compassion for the maiden.'

statements.claim: Arjuna solved the riddle like a man striking a serpent coiled around a camel, wounding the demon with his thin arrows without ever touching the girl.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (17-18): 'As when a serpent gets round a camel, a man... strikes the serpent leaving the camel to itself, so Partha, the foremost of archers, began to strike the Daitya with his arrows... wounded the Danavas with their cane-like arrows.'

statements.claim: By his illusory powers Nikumbha vanished with the maiden so completely that none could tell where they had gone, assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture as he fled.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (19-20): 'resorting to his illusory powers Nikumbha so disappeared with the maiden... he, however, went on assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture.'

statements.claim: The chase carried them across all seven continents of the earth until Nikumbha dropped onto the summit of Mount Gokarna, on the bank of the river Chela Ganga, which no god, Asura or ascetic could cross, being guarded by the energy of Mahadeva.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (22-24): 'travelled all over the earth consisting of seven insular continents and dropped down... on the bank of the river Chela Ganga flowing on the summit of the mount Gokarna. None amongst the gods, Asuras or great ascetics could cross that mountain protected by the energy of Mahadeva.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, a master of illusion himself, snatched Bhanumati away while Krishna and Arjuna assailed the demon, who fled from the northern range of Gokarna to the southern.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (25-26): 'Finding this weak point of Nikumbha, the Bhaima chief Pradyumna... got hold of the maiden Bhanumati. And Krishna, and Arjuna began to assail the Asura greatly with arrows. Then leaving the northern range of the mount Gokarna, Nikumbha fled to the southern range.'

statements.claim: With Krishna's permission Pradyumna carried the maiden home to Dwaraka and returned to find Krishna and Arjuna at the mouth of the cave that was the entrance to Shatpura, Nikumbha's city.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (26-29): 'the great Asura entered into Shatpura, the abode of his kinsmen... With Krishna's permission the heroic son of Rukshmini... took... the maiden to the city of Dwaraka. And keeping her there he returned to Shatpura... and beheld the two Krishnas... at the mouth of the cave.'

statements.claim: All night the three kept watch at the cave's mouth; at dawn the demon came out to fight.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (27-30) says 'those two heroes spent the night at the mouth of the cave' (Krishna and Arjuna) while Pradyumna was taking the maiden to Dwaraka, then all three 'waited there with Pradyumna' at the entrance. Minor timeline compression, no contradiction of events.

statements.claim: At dawn Nikumbha broke through Arjuna's Gandiva arrows, struck him on the head with his thorn-covered club; the hero vomited blood and lost consciousness, and the master of illusions carried him off.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 (31-33): 'Dhananjaya, with arrows shot off his Gandiva bow, obstructed the thorough-fair. In spite of it Nikumbha... took up his club covered with thorns and struck Partha on his head. Thus assailed... Pritha's son vomitted blood and lost his consciousness.' Arjuna's abduction confirmed by pack summary: Krishna 'frees the abducted Arjuna.'

statements.claim: Thousands of Nikumbhas filled earth and sky, but Krishna perceived the true form of the creator of illusions and cut off his head with the discus, whereupon every false form dissolved and Arjuna was free.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, HV 1.237: 'they saw all over the earth and welkin thousands of Nikumbha... the Divine Lord Krishna... saw the true form of Nikumbha, the creator of illusions... with his discus, cut off his head'; index title: 'Krishna Destroys a Body of Nikumbha with the Discus... frees the abducted Arjuna.'

statements.claim: Krishna gathered Arjuna onto Garuda and turned toward Dwaraka, leaving Shatpura's master destroyed.
statements.evidence: Closing connective narration consistent with the pack outcome (Nikumbha's head cut off, Arjuna freed); the specific departure scene is not in the visible passage.

notes: Fully grounded in HV 1.237. Minor compression: the night watch at the cave mouth is attributed to all three though the source places it on Krishna and Arjuna with Pradyumna rejoining; treated as connective. Atmosphere (smiles, weeping, dawn) is narrative texture.

statements.claim: Vajranabha practised hard austerities on the summit of Mount Sumeru, and pleased Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, asked him to pray for a boon.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (5-6): 'a great Asura, celebrated by the name of Vajranabha, practised hard austerities on the summit of the mount Sumeru. Pleased with his penances the Divine Brahma, the grand-father of the world, asked him to pray for a boon.'

statements.claim: Vajranabha asked two gifts: that even the gods might never kill him, and that he might possess the city Vajra, where even the air could not enter without his will, a city that gave its lord whatever he desired unasked, ringed by gardens and walls, surrounded by branch cities, full of peerless gems.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (7-9): 'prayed for two boons that even the gods might not kill him, and that he might get the city Vajra where even the air cannot easily enter, which gives every sort of desired-for objects even when they are not thought of, which has gardens encircled by walls, many branch cities, and peerless jems of every description'; the 'without his will' condition appears at 1.238 (23): 'even the wind cannot enter into his city if Vajranabha does not wish it.'

statements.claim: Brahma granted both, Vajranabha lived in Vajra, and millions of demons dwelt there in his garden and the branch cities, healthy, well-fed and contented.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (10-12): 'By that boon he got what he wanted and the great Asura Vajranabha lived in the city of Vajra... millions of demons lived in that city of Vajra, in his garden and in many charming branch cities... healthy, well-fed and contented.'

statements.claim: Elated by pride in his boon, Vajranabha told Indra: 'All the three worlds are the common property of the high-souled sons of Kashyapa. I wish to govern the three worlds. If you do not approve of my proposal, give me battle.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (13-15), near-verbatim quotation of the source.

statements.claim: Indra consulted Brihaspati and answered that their father, the ascetic Kashyapa, was engaged in a sacrifice and would do what is fair after its termination.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (16-17): 'Mahendra... consulted with Vrihaspati and said... our father, the ascetic Kashyapa, is now engaged in a sacrifice. After its termination he will do what is fair.'

statements.claim: Vajranabha carried the same demand to Kashyapa, who repeated Indra's words and told him to return to Vajra, live self-controlled, and wait for the sacrifice to end.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (18-19): 'Kashyapa said what the king of gods had communicated... O son, go now to the city of Vajra and live there controlling yourself. After the termination of the Yajna I will do what is fair.'

statements.claim: Indra went secretly to Dwaraka and told Krishna everything Vajranabha had said.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (20): 'Mahendra went to the city of Dwaravati... and communicated secretly to Vasudeva what Vajranabha had said.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered: 'My father's horse-sacrifice is at hand. When it is over, I will kill Vajranabha. But even the wind cannot enter his city unless he wishes it, so we will find our own way in.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (20-23): 'the horse-sacrifice of Vasudeva is now at hand. After its termination I will kill Vajranabha... even the wind cannot enter into his city if Vajranabha does not wish it. At a convenient hour we will concert measures for entering there.' (Vasudeva is Krishna's father, so 'my father's horse-sacrifice' is accurate.)

statements.claim: During the horse-sacrifice the actor Bhadra pleased the assembled sages with his art and was asked to pray for a boon.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (26-27): 'During the celebration of Vasudeva's sacrifice an actor, by name Bhadra, pleased the great saints with his beautiful acting. The leading Munis then asked him to pray for a boon.'

statements.claim: Prompted by Krishna's wish and as if urged by the goddess of learning, Bhadra asked to range freely over the earth and sky, to be slain by no creature mobile or immobile, to assume any form, never to be touched by age, and to find the sages always pleased with him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (28-32): 'as desired by Krishna and as if urged on by the goddess of learning, prayed for the following boon... may I range over the earth consisting of seven insular continents... range all over the sky... be not slain by all creatures mobile and immobile. May I assume any form... May not decrepitude overtake me and may the Munis always remain pleased with me.' (The story's list is selective, omitting the first boon about the food of the twice-born — not contradictory.)

statements.claim: The Munis said 'So be it,' and Bhadra wandered the cities of the demon kings performing, coming to Dwaraka on every festival day where the Yadavas received him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (33-35): 'the Munis said So be it... He began to show his performances in the cities of the Danava kings... On the occasion of every Parva, that great actor... used to come to Dwaraka adorned with the Yadavas.'

statements.claim: In heaven Indra told the swans — his brothers, begotten by Kashyapa, though carriers of the gods and the pious — of the great duty of killing the enemies of the gods.
statements.evidence: HV 1.238 (36-37): 'Sakra... said to Dhartarashtra swans: O celestial birds, although you are the carriers of the gods and the pious, still you are our brothers on account of your being begotten by Kashyapa... Now the great duty of killing the enemies of the gods awa...' (source text truncated at this point but matches).

notes: Grounded in HV 1.238. 'No enemy had ever been known to pass those walls' is rhetorical connective framing of the wind-proof city. Boon list summarized selectively but accurately.

statements.claim: The troupe's fame ran ahead of them in the lands of the demons, and the Asuras welcomed the actor with presents of jewels.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (3-4): 'arriving there, the actors too, heard of before, excited their curiosity... With great delight they welcomed the actor with presents of jewels.'

statements.claim: In the city of Supura the citizens were so enchanted they begged for more.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (5): 'the actor, who had obtained the boon, pleased highly the citizens of Supura with his dancing.' The delighted response is supported; 'begged for more' is an embellishment of their enthusiasm.

statements.claim: The troupe's newest players were Pradyumna, Gada, Shamba and other Yadava heroes in costumes, led by Bhadra, the actor granted the boon to wander the three worlds.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (15-16): 'the Daityas, living in branch cities, took the Yadavas, disguised as actors, to the charming city of Vajra'; Bhadra's world-ranging boon is from HV 1.238 (29-32).

statements.claim: Vajranabha, having heard of the marvellous actors, sent a messenger to bring the actor in.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (14): 'the king of Daityas had already heard of it. Now pleased he sent a messenger to bring the actor.'

statements.claim: The demons of the branch cities brought the troupe to Vajra, lodged them in a house built by the celestial architect, and supplied needed articles by the hundred.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (15-17): 'the Daityas, living in branch cities, took the Yadavas... to the charming city of Vajra. For their accomodation, a beautiful house, built by the celestial architect, was offered, and necessary articles, by hundreds, were given them.'

statements.claim: Vajranabha set up a beautiful pavilion and made a festival with the actors; his family's women watched from behind a screen where they could see all, while he sat with his kinsmen.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (18-20): 'having set up a beautiful pandal the great Asura, Vajranabha, made a great festival with the actors... having kept the women of his family behind a screen at a place from which they could see all, the great Asura himself sat with his kinsmen.'

statements.claim: First the instruments — bells, flutes, drums — then the women of the troupe sang the celestial Gandharva song Chhalikya, the music the Yadavas had brought down from heaven.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (21-23): 'They first played various tunes on musical instruments, as Kansya, Venu, Muraja etc. Afterwards the women, brought by the Bhaimas, sang the Gandharva song Chhalikya'; its celestial origin is the corpus chain (DKS_0241: 'Krishna Brings the Celestial Chhalikya Song to the Yadavas').

statements.claim: They sang the descent of the Ganga in seven scales and three modes, in the raga Vasanta and its kin, and the Asuras rose again and again to please the actors.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (24-25): 'with seven scales, Gandhara and others, three Gramas, and with Ragas, Vasanta and others, they sang sweetly the song of the sacred discension of Ganga... Asuras rose up again and again and pleased the actors.'

statements.claim: They performed the Ramayana: the birth of Vishnu for the destruction of Ravana, and how the sage Rishyashringa was brought to King Dasharatha.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (6-7): 'They gave a performance of the great epic Ramayana: the birth of the incomparable Vishnu for the destruction of the king of Rakshasas (Ravana). How Lomapada and Dasharatha had brought for Shanta, the Muni Rishwashringa.' The story's phrasing compresses the well-known episode (Rishyashringa fetched, later serving Dasharatha's sacrifice) without contradicting it.

statements.claim: The demons were startled that actors could so resemble Rama, Lakshmana and Bharata, and repeatedly rose to give away necklaces of gold and vaidurya, bracelets and cloths.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (8-13): 'the actors so perfectly personated the characters of Rama, Lakshmana, Shatrughna, Bharata... that even the elderly Danavas were startled... they repeatedly rose up, expressed their appreciation and gave away charming necklaces of gold and Vaidurja, bracelets and cloths.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, in actor's guise, conducted the prologue with Gada and Shamba, and Rukmini's son sang the hymn of the Ganga's descent with beautiful gestures.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (26): 'the powerful Pradyumna, who had assumed the guise of an actor, Gada and Shamva conducted the Nandi. After the termination of the Prologue Rukshmini's son sang the hymn, accompanied with beautiful gestures, of the descension of Ganga.' (Pradyumna is Rukmini's son — consistent.)

statements.claim: In the drama Rambhabhisara, Shura played Ravana, Monovati Rambha, Pradyumna Nalakuvara and Shamba his jester; by illusion the Yadavas conjured the scene of Kailasha and acted Nalakuvara cursing Ravana and consoling Rambha.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (27-30): 'they began the performance of the drama Rambhabhisara, Shura acted the part of Ravana, Monovati represented Rambha, Pradyumna Nalakuvara and Shamva his Vidushaka. By their illusory powers the Yadavas represented the scene of Kailasha. They acted how the wicked Ravana was imprecated by Nalakuvara... and how Rambha was consoled.'

statements.claim: The Danavas gave costly garments, jewelled necklaces, sky-going cars, celestial elephants, sandal, aguru and scents, and the gem Chintamani which grants all that is thought of — until the demon lords were deprived of their riches and jewels, their women too.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (31-37): 'They gave them costly apparels, jewelleries, necklaces set with costly jems... cars ranging in the sky, elephants coursing in the etherial region, cool and celestial sandal, Agura, and other scents and the valuable jem Chintamani which gives all that is thought of. Giving away presents in this way at every scene those Danavas were deprived of their riches and jewels. Even the women of the Danava-Chiefs shared the same fate.' ('Treasuries ran dry' is the source's 'deprived of their riches' rendered vividly.)

statements.claim: Behind the screen Prabhavati received Suchimukhi's message: she had gone to Dwaraka, seen Pradyumna secretly, told him of Prabhavati's love, and he had appointed this evening to meet her — for the Bhaimas never speak untruth.
statements.evidence: HV 1.240 (38-41): 'Prabhavati's friend Suchimukhi said to her... I had gone to the charming city of Dwaraka... I saw Pradyumna there secretly and told him about your love for him... Pleased he has appointed this evening for meeting you... the Bhaimas never speak an untruth; verily to-day you will meet your love.' (Suchimukhi is the goose addressed in the following verse.)

notes: Grounded in HV 1.240. 'The city of Vajra was impossible to enter / even the wind could not pass unless willed' rests on HV 1.238 (23), carried by the corpus chain. Only flourish: Supura citizens 'begged for more'. Performance details map 1:1 to the source.

statements.claim: After Kashyapa's sacrifice ended, the gods and Asuras returned to their habitations.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (1): 'After the termination of the sacrifice of Kashyapa... the gods and Asuras repaired to their respective habitations.'

statements.claim: Vajranabha went to Kashyapa to set the conquest of the three worlds in motion and received a warning.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (2): 'After the end of the sacrifice Vajranabha too, desirous of conquering the three worlds, went to Kashyapa who told him...'

statements.claim: Kashyapa's warning: Sakra is the eldest and foremost, endued with ascetic power, devoted to the Brahmanas, grateful, king of the whole world, refuge of the good and pious, ruling because he works for the well-being of all creatures; Vajranabha will not vanquish him but will himself be killed, as one who rouses a serpent is destroyed in no time.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (3-6), near-verbatim: 'Sakra is the eldest of you all and the foremost in accomplishments... Because he is engaged in the well-being of all creatures he has obtained this sovereignty over the world. O Vajranabha, you will not be able to vanquish him but yourself will be killed. As one who excites the anger of a serpent meets with his own destruction, so you will in no time be destroyed.'

statements.claim: Vajranabha refused his father's counsel, saluted Kashyapa, and began arrangements, gathering kinsmen, warriors and friends, first setting out to conquer the region of the celestials.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (7-9): 'as a man, desirous of meeting with death... does not take medicine so Vajranabha did not approve of the words of Kashyapa. Having saluted Kashyapa... he collected his kinsmen, warriors, and friends. He first set out for conquering the region of the celestials.'

statements.claim: Indra and Upendra had sent the swans, birds begotten by Kashyapa and brothers of the gods, to bring about Vajranabha's destruction.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (10): 'the highly powerful deities Indra and Upendra had sent the Swans there for bringing about Vajranabha's destruction'; their Kashyapa-begotten brotherhood is from HV 1.238 (36-37).

statements.claim: Learning from the swans that Vajranabha was marching, the Yadavas worried: Vajranabha will be killed by Pradyumna, but Vajranabha's daughter and Sunabha's daughters, their devoted wives, are all with child and near delivery.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (11-14): 'the high-souled... Yadus thus consulted... Forsooth Vajranabha will be killed now by Pradyumna. But Vajranabha's daughter and Sunabha's daughters are their devoted wives. They are all enciente and the time for their delivery is near at hand.'

statements.claim: The gods promised through the swans: you will have beautiful sons like Kama, who even in the womb will master the Vedas with their auxiliaries, grow to youth at once, and master every future topic and scripture.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (15-17), near-verbatim.

statements.claim: In Vajra, Prabhavati bore Pradyumna a son, omniscient and youthful like his father; after a month Chandravati bore Chandraprabha, resembling Gada; and Gunavati bore Gunavan — all youthful and omniscient.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (19-21): 'Prabhavati gave birth to a son, omniscient and youthful after his father. The son Chandraprabha, resembling Gada, whom Chandravati gave birth to after a month... Gunavati too gave birth to a similiarly beautiful son by name Gunavan, youthful and omniscient.'

statements.claim: The boys mastered every shastra and moved about the palace turrets, shown to the Daityas by the desire of Indra and Upendra.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (22-23): 'These Yadu boys began to grow up... mastering all the Shastras. They used to move about on the turrets of the palaces and at the desire of Indra and Upendra they were seen (by the Daityas).'

statements.claim: The Daityas stationed in the sky told Vajranabha, who cried 'Arrest them who have trespassed into my house'; soldiers guarded all quarters amid cries to seize and kill them, and the mothers wept.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (24-27): 'As soon as they saw them the Daityas, stationed in the sky... communicated it to Vajranabha... Vajranabha said: Arrest them who have trespassed into my house... the soldiers guarded all the quarters... exclamations, Arrest them speedily kill them. Hearing it the mothers, fond of sons, began to weep in fear.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna reassured them: so long as we are alive and firm, the Daityas can do nothing to us.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (28-29), near-verbatim.

statements.claim: Pradyumna told Prabhavati her father, uncles, brothers and kinsmen waited with clubs; for her sake they deserve respect, but the time is dreadful — if they endure they die, if they fight they succeed — and asked her to consult her two sisters, being under her orders.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (30-33), near-verbatim.

statements.claim: Prabhavati, kneeling and weeping with hands on her forehead, urged him to take up arms: if he survives he will see his wife and sons; remember the honourable Rukmini and Aniruddha; a great rishi booned her a blameless life, no widowhood and living sons, and she hopes his words will not be falsified; she rinsed her mouth and placed a sword in his hands.
statements.evidence: HV 1.243 (34-38): 'Placing her hands on her forehead and kneeling down Prabhavati, weeping, said... take up your arms and protect yourself. If you yourself survive you will see your wife and sons. Remember the honarable Vaidarbhi and Aniruddha... the great and intelligent Rishi had conferred on me the boon that I would lead a blameless life for ever, would not be a widow and my sons would live... Saying this and rinsing her month... handed over a sword to Rukshmini's son.' (Vaidarbhi = Rukmini.)

notes: Grounded in HV 1.243 with near-verbatim dialogue. The opening's 'went home to prepare' before visiting Kashyapa is a light connective reordering of verse 2 (he goes to Kashyapa straight after the sacrifice).

statements.claim: From Garuda's back Krishna saw his own house of hundreds of palaces, the sable-hued palace, with a million white jewelled pillars, a gate of gems lustrous as fire and golden seats set here and there.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (1-8): 'saw his own house consisting of hundreds of palaces. He saw there a million of white jewelled pillars, a gate with jems lustrous like fire and a number of effulgent golden seats placed here and there... sable-hued palace.'

statements.claim: For his court a great palace entirely of gold with crystal pillars was made, ringed by lakes full of lotuses and fragrant red lotuses, maddened peacocks and coels, with golden and jewelled stairways.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (5-6): 'a huge palace had been made entirely of gold with crystal pillars. He also saw beautiful and big lakes, with its water full of lotuses and fragrant red lotuses resorted to by maddened peacocks and coels, with golden and jewelled stairs.'

statements.claim: Viswakarma enclosed the whole with stone walls a hundred yards high girded with ditches, on a plot half a yojana on every side, measured against Indra's palace.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (7-8): 'That house was encircled by Viswakarma with stone walls hundred yards high which were girt with ditches. After the measurement of Indra's palace the celestial Architect had built that house on a plot of land measuring half a yojana on all sides.'

statements.claim: Krishna blew the Panchajanya: the sound made his enemies' hairs stand erect, stirred the ocean, resounded through the sky, and seemed most wonderful.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (9-10): 'He then blew his conch the sound of which made the hairs of his enemies stand erect. At that sound the ocean was greatly agitated and the sky resounded. Indeed it appeared very wonderful... Hearing the sound of Panchajanya conch-shell...'

statements.claim: At the conch's sound and the sight of Garuda, the Kukuras and Andhakas were freed from sorrow; beholding Keshava shining like the sun with conch, discus and club, the citizens beat trumpets, blew bugles and raised leonine shouts.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (10-13): 'Hearing the sound of Panchajanya conch-shell and seeing Garuda all the members of the Kukura and Andhaka families were freed from sorrow. Beholding Keshava effulgent like the sun, with conch-shell, discus, and club in his hands, seated on Garuda, the citizens attained to an excess of joy. Thereupon they began to beat trumpets, blew bugles and set up leonine shouts.'

statements.claim: Beholding the slayer of Madhu, the Kukuras, Andhakas and other Dasharhas approached him with great delight.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (13): 'beholding the slayer of Madhu the Kukuras, Andhakas and other Dasharhas began to approach him with great delight.'

statements.claim: King Ugrasena, placing Vasudeva before him, repaired to Vasudeva's palace with conches and trumpets; Devaki, Rohini and Ahuka's wives moved about with joy.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (14-15): 'Placing Vasudeva before him and accompanied with the sound of conch-shells and trumpets, the king Ugrasena repaired to Vasudeva's palace. Devaki, Rohini and Ahuka's wives began to move about with joy in their own houses.'

statements.claim: Hari, whom Indra and the other gods serve, arrived at the appointed house; alighting at the entrance he showed respect to the Yadus and, honored by Balarama, Ahuka, Gada and Pradyumna, entered his residence with the mountain of jewels.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (16-18): 'Hari whom serve Indra and other gods, arrived at the appointed house. Having got down at the entrance... showed proper respect to all the Yadus. And himself honored by Rama, Ahuka, Gada, Pradyumna and others he entered into his residence with the mountain of jewels.'

statements.claim: Rukmini's son Pradyumna carried in the Parijata, the tree most favourite of Indra; by its power the heroes saw the beauty of their own persons and delighted.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (19-20): 'Rukshmini's son Pradyumna himself took to the house the Parijata the most favourite of Indra's trees. By the power of the Parijata the heroes saw the beauty of their own persons and attained to great delight.'

statements.claim: Eulogized by the Yadu chiefs, Krishna entered the house Viswakarma built, placed the jewel-mountain in his inner apartment, and with the Vrishnis worshipped and planted the Parijata in its proper place.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (21): 'Thus eulogized by the delighted Yadu chiefs Krishna entered into the house constructed by Viswakarma. Having placed that mountain of jems with summits in his inner appartment Achyuta... united with the Vrishnis, worshipped the celestial tree Parijata and planted it in its proper place.'

statements.claim: With his kinsmen's permission Krishna honored all the maidens brought from Naraka's house with raiments, ornaments, maid-servants, riches and objects of enjoyment; they had already been received by Devaki, Rohini, Revati and Ahuka's wives.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (22-24): 'obtaining the permission of his own kinsmen Keshava... honored all the maidens he had brought from Naraka's house with raiments, ornaments, maid-servants, riches and objects of enjoyment. Those maidens had already been received honourably by Devaki, Rohini, Revati and Ahuka's wives.'

statements.claim: By his good fortune Satyabhama ruled over all the females, while Rukmini, Bhishmaka's daughter, was in charge of the relatives, and Krishna allotted each woman her own house, tank and garden.
statements.evidence: HV 1.246 (25-28): 'By his good luck Satyabhama ruled over all the females, and Bhishmaka's daughter Rukshmini was in charge of the relatives. Krishna allotted to each of those women, separate houses, tanks, and gardens.'

notes: Grounded in HV 1.246, nearly scene-by-scene. Final paragraph (Parijata 'changing the air of the city', jewel-mountain 'like a promise kept') is connective close on supported elements. 'Dwarka'/'Dwaraka' spelling variance only.

statements.claim: Balarama, Rohini's son, grew dreadful like Kala at the end of a cycle, drew enemies close with his ploughshare and ground them with his mace.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (65-66): 'when Rohini's son engaged in the battle his form grew dreadful like Kala, as if desirous of consuming all, at the end of a cycle. Ranging in the battle-field the highly powerful Baladeva... drew the enemies with his plough-share and grinded them with his mace.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna thwarted the fighting Danavas with his arrows; Krishna, dark as a mass of collyrium, blew his conch and fought in many ways with conch, discus and club.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (67-68): 'The highly powerful Pradyumna... thwarted the fighting Danavas with his arrows. Blowing his conch-shell Janarddana, the holder of conch-shell, discus and club, resembling a mass of collyrium, fought in many ways.'

statements.claim: Garuda struck the Daityas with his wings and mutilated them with beak and nails, despatching them to Yama's abode; overpowered by those four heroes the Asura army fled.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (69-70): 'Having struck the Daityas with his wings and mutilated them with his nails and beak the intelligent son of Vinata despatched them to the abode of Yama. Thus assailed with a downpour of arrows and overpowered by those four heroes the dreadful army of the Asuras fled away.'

statements.claim: Seeing his host routed, Rudra's follower Jvara, the fever-demon, came walking to the field sighing like a maniac; he had three legs, three heads, six arms, nine faces and a consuming weapon, like Yama himself.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (71-72): 'Rudra's follower, Jvara, came walking to the battle-field sighing again and again like a maniac. He had three legs, three heads, six arms, nine faces and a consuming weapon and was like Yama himself.'

statements.claim: He roared like thousands of muttering clouds, yawned and dozed, hairs erect, eyes filthy; making his face terrible, he told the wielder of the ploughshare he would not return with his life.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (73-75): 'He roared like thousands of muttering clouds, sighed and yawned repeatedly, was dozing, had his hairs erect and eyes filthy... Why are you elated with the pride of your strength? Do you not see that I have come to the battle-field? Wait a few moments. While you have come before me in the battle-field you will not return with your life.'

statements.claim: Smiling and showing a fist dreadful as the fire of dissolution, Jvara ran at Balarama, who wheeled in thousands of circular ways so the demon found no opening.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (76): 'smiling and showing his fist dreadful like the fire of dissolution Jvara ran towards Halayudha. Rohini's son however began to move about so quickly in thousands of circular ways that Jvara could not find an opportunity.'

statements.claim: Jvara's consuming weapon struck Balarama's breast, fell onto Mount Sumeru shattering it into pieces, and the remnant left on his breast began to consume Krishna's elder brother.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (77-78): 'hurled his consuming weapon which fell on his breast. Dropping on the summit of the mount Sumeru from Rama's breast that burning weapon shattered it into pieces. Krishna's elder brother was however being consumed by the remnant that was left on his breast.'

statements.claim: Sighing and yawning ceaselessly, eyes dilated, hairs erect, senses bewildered, almost losing consciousness, Balarama cried to Krishna: 'I am being consumed... How shall I be saved?'
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (79-84): 'His eyes were dilated, hairs stood erect and all his senses were bewildered... almost losing consciousness Haladhara said to Krishna:—O Krishna, O large-armed Krishna, O thou the giver of protection, I am being consumed, nay I am being consumed completely. How shall I be saved?'

statements.claim: Krishna smiled, said 'No fear', and embraced his brother, who was thereby saved from being burnt.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (84): 'Krishna... smilingly said:—No fear. Saying this he embraced Halayudha. He was then saved by loving Krishna from being burnt.'

statements.claim: The slayer of Madhu, highly angered, told Jvara: 'Come and fight with me. Show me the full extent of your strength and power in this battle.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (84): 'Having saved Rama from being consumed the slayer of Madhu, Vasudeva, highly angered, said to Jvara:—O Jvara, come and fight with me. Show to me the extent of your strength and power in this battle.'

notes: Grounded in HV 1.270 (Sonitpura battlefield per pack index; story leaves the field unnamed). Opening and closing lines are connective framing of supported battle events.

statements.claim: Recap: Jvara came to protect the routed Asura army; his burning weapon fell on Balarama's breast and consumed him; Krishna saved his brother with an embrace and the fire went out.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (70-84), fully present in this pack: 'with a view to protect them Rudra's follower, Jvara, came walking to the battle-field... hurled his consuming weapon which fell on his breast... Krishna's elder brother was however being consumed... he embraced Halayudha. He was then saved by loving Krishna from being burnt.'

statements.claim: Krishna challenged Jvara to show the extent of his strength and power in the battle.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (84): 'O Jvara, come and fight with me. Show to me the extent of your strength and power in this battle.'

statements.claim: Jvara, three-legged, three-headed, six-armed, nine-faced, follower of Rudra, discharged his great burning weapon with his right hand at Krishna's body; Krishna felt the burning for a few moments and then the fire went out.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (85-86): 'Jvara, with his right hand, discharged his great burning weapon on Krishna's body. At this the powerful Krishna, the foremost of strikers, experienced a burning sensation for a few moments. Immediately after the fire was put out.' ('The way fire dies when it meets what it cannot consume' is connective imagery.)

statements.claim: Jvara, with serpent-like long arms, struck Krishna on the neck and dealt a blow on his breast; a great encounter followed between the fever-demon and the foremost of men.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (87-89): 'Jvara, with his serpent-like long arms, struck Krishna on the neck and then dealt a blow on his breast. Thus there took place a great encounter, in the battle-field, between Jvara and the highly energetic Krishna the foremost of men.'

statements.claim: The sound of their striking arms was like thunder striking a mountain summit.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (89): 'The sound of the stricking of arms caused by Krishna and Jvara in that highly dreadful battle was like that of a thunder striking a mountain summit.'

statements.claim: In the midst of the fight were heard words as if one fighter instructed the other: 'Do not strike this way. Strike this way.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (90): 'Occasionally was heard Do not strike in this way: you should do it in this way.'

statements.claim: The Lord of the Universe, under the guise of a man, as if thinking he would come to an end, ground the sky-ranging, golden-adorned Jvara with his arms in a fearful struggle.
statements.evidence: HV 1.270 (91-93): 'that Lord of the Universe, under the guise of a man, thinking that he would come to an end, grinded the sky-ranging Jvara adorned with golden ornaments with his arms.' (The pestle-and-mortar simile and 'strength ran out like water from a broken jar' are narrative imagery for the grinding, which the source records.)

statements.claim: The two fought for a moment, and Krishna threw the broken Jvara down upon the earth, believing the field was won.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (1) (corpus-chain next event, in DKS_0249's pack): 'Considering Jvara, assailed with his arms, dead Krishna... threw him down on the surface of the earth.' Consistent with the close of 1.270.

statements.claim: Released from the crushing embrace, the fever-demon did not flee but entered Krishna's body.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (2): 'Released from his arms, Jvara, of incomparable energy, did not leave Krishna's body but entered into it.' (Presented here as cliffhanger leading to DKS_0249.)

notes: Grounded in HV 1.270, with the closing possession taken from the immediately following HV 1.271 (canonical next event). 'Field emptied around them' is connective. 'Two most powerful beings... strokes that would have felled armies' is rhetorical amplification of the source's language, not a new fact.

statements.claim: Considering Jvara dead from the grinding of his arms, Krishna threw him down on the earth, but released from his grip the fever-demon of incomparable energy entered Krishna's body.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (1-2): 'Considering Jvara, assailed with his arms, dead Krishna... threw him down on the surface of the earth. Released from his arms, Jvara, of incomparable energy, did not leave Krishna's body but entered into it.'

statements.claim: Possessed by fever, Krishna's movements slackened; he repeatedly supported himself by touching the ground, was possessed by sleep, his steps slackened, hairs stood erect, and he sighed and yawned repeatedly.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (3-4): 'Possessed by Jvara (fever) of incomparable energy Krishna had his movements slackened and repeatedly supported himself by touching the ground. He was possessed by sleep, his steps were slackened and his hairs stood erect. He repeatedly sighed and yawned.'

statements.claim: The great Yogin, victor of enemy cities, regained his natural state only after a long time.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (5): 'the great Yogin Krishna, the victor of the enemy's cities, regained his natural state after a long time.'

statements.claim: Knowing himself possessed, Krishna created from his own energy a dreadful second Jvara, terrible to all creatures, for the destruction of the first.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (6-8): 'knowing himself possessed by Jvara Purosottama created another for its destruction. With his energy... created a dreadful Jvara, highly terrible unto creatures.'

statements.claim: The created fever seized the first Jvara by force, dragged him out of Krishna's body, and presented him before his maker — the fever was driven out by fever itself.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (8-9): 'Catching hold, by force, of the former Jvara the one, created by Krishna, presented it before him. Having thus driven out that Jvara from his body through one created by him...'

statements.claim: The angry Krishna struck Jvara down and was about to tear him to pieces; bewildered, Jvara cried 'O Janardana, it behooves you to protect me!'
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (10): 'the highly powerful and angry Vasudeva struck him down on the ground and was about to tear him into pieces. Thereat Jvara, bewildered, said O Janarddana, it behoveth thee to protect me.'

statements.claim: An invisible voice from the sky commanded: 'O Krishna... the delight of the Yadavas, do not kill this Jvara. O sinless one, he is worthy of being protected by you.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (11-12): 'an invisible voice was heard in the sky:—O Krishna, O large-armed Krishna, the enhancer of the delight of the Yadavas, do not kill this Jvara. O sinless one, he is worthy of being protected by thee.'

statements.claim: Hari, lord of the past, future and present, great preceptor of the world, let Jvara go.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (12): 'Thus addressed Hari, the lord of the past, future and present and the great preceptor of the world let Jvara off.'

statements.claim: Jvara prostrated with bent head at Krishna's feet and asked the boon that he alone be the fever in this world, with no other flourishing beside him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (13-15): 'prostrating himself with bent head at Hrishikesha's feet Jvara said... I pray from thee for this boon only that I may be the only Jvara in this world and no one else may flourish.'

statements.claim: Krishna granted it: it is proper to confer a boon on one who prays; as before Jvara will be the only fever, and he whom Krishna created will dissolve into him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (16-18): 'It is proper to confer a boon on one who prays for it. Besides you have sought my protection... As before you will be the only Jvara. May he, whom I have created, dissolve in me.'

statements.claim: Krishna told Jvara how he would range through the world, and promised that whoever, having saluted Krishna, attentively reads this account of the great battle will be freed from fever.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (19-28, 33-35): Krishna instructs how Jvara will range spread among creation mobile and immobile, and 'the man, who having saluted me, will attentively read this account of prowess displayed only by our arms in the great battle, will be freed from fever.'

statements.claim: Jvara, delighted, said 'So be it' and, saluting his master, left the battlefield.
statements.evidence: HV 1.271 (36-37): 'the highly powerful Jvara said:—So be it. Having thus obtained the boon and promised, Jvara, saluting Krishna, left the battle-field.'

notes: Grounded in HV 1.271 with near-verbatim boon exchange. 'As everything made from him returns to him' is theological connective gloss on the created Jvara dissolving into Krishna. The story omits the detailed four-part division of fever among creatures — an omission, not a distortion.
